title: Doval Reveals Modi's First Response at Airport After Pahalgam Terror Attack in New Docuseries
excerpt: Discovery's 'Declassified: Operation Sindoor,' premiering on India's Independence Day, features NSA Ajit Doval and military chiefs recounting the 88-hour conflict that followed the deadly Pahalgam attack.
body:
• Discovery's two-part docuseries 'Declassified: Operation Sindoor' premieres August 15, 2026, featuring first-hand accounts from NSA Doval and all three service chiefs
  • PM Modi cut short his Saudi Arabia visit after the April 22, 2025 Pahalgam attack that killed 26 people, convening a high-level meeting at Palam airport with Doval and Jaishankar
  • Doval personally took command of strike planning, keeping final target lists known only to himself until two hours before launch
  • Operation Sindoor struck nine terror locations across seven cities in Pakistan and PoK in a 25-minute pre-dawn offensive on May 7, 2025

National Security Advisor Ajit Doval has offered a detailed account of PM Narendra Modi's immediate response to the Pahalgam terror attack in a new Discovery docuseries set to premiere on India's 80th Independence Day, revealing previously undisclosed details about the decision-making chain that led to Operation Sindoor.

The two-part documentary, titled 'Declassified: Operation Sindoor,' will air on Discovery and discovery+ on August 15, 2026, with part one at 9 PM and part two at 10 PM. It marks the launch of Discovery's new Declassified franchise focused on pivotal historical moments.

The Airport Meeting That Set Events in Motion

On April 22, 2025, terrorists from The Resistance Front — a Pakistan-based outfit linked to Lashkar-e-Taiba — opened fire on tourists in the Baisaran Valley near Pahalgam, killing 26 people including two foreign nationals. PM Modi, who was in Jeddah for the India-Saudi Arabia Strategic Partnership Council, immediately cancelled a scheduled state dinner and his address to the Indian community, flying back to New Delhi.

https://x.com/timesofindia/status/2088203991544979554

Upon landing at Palam airport, Modi convened a high-level security briefing attended by Doval, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, and Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri. According to accounts featured in the docuseries, Modi's focus was immediate and operational — he wanted to understand the full scope of the attack and India's options for response.

Modi subsequently gave the armed forces "complete operational freedom" and stated publicly that the terrorists and their backers would be pursued "to the ends of the earth."

Doval's Command of the Strike Planning

The docuseries reveals the extent of Doval's hands-on role in planning the retaliatory operation. According to government sources cited by News18, Doval supervised the strategic framework and ensured execution remained tightly controlled, with secrecy, surprise, and escalation management at its core.

"Don't mistake India's generosity with weakness."

— Ajit Doval, National Security Advisor

On May 3, the 11th day after the Pahalgam attack, a critical meeting at South Block brought together Modi, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi, Air Force Chief Marshal Amarpreet Singh, and Navy Chief Admiral Dinesh Kumar Tripathi. The decision to strike terrorist locations in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir was taken. Doval selected officers from all three services and moved the planning team into South Block.

By May 5, the attack plan was presented to Modi. Until two hours before launch, the final list of targets was known only to Doval — multiple target lists had been prepared, with last-minute changes made to maximize tactical advantage.

The 25-Minute Operation

At 1:05 AM on May 7, 2025, the Indian Air Force launched Operation Sindoor. In 25 minutes, nine terror infrastructure sites across seven cities in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir were struck using BrahMos and Akash missiles. The targets included training camps and command centers linked to Jaish-e-Mohammed and Lashkar-e-Taiba.

The docuseries features key military voices including Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan, Lt. Gen. Rajiv Ghai (Director General Military Operations), and Lt. Gen. Pratik Sharma (Northern Army Command), offering what Warner Bros. Discovery called "unprecedented access" to the individuals in war rooms and on the frontlines during the 88-hour conflict between two nuclear-armed nations.

Doval's Message to the World

In a speech at IIT Madras following the operation, Doval challenged global media to produce even a single image showing damage to Indian infrastructure. "You tell me one photograph, one image, showing any Indian infrastructure hit? Even a glass pane?" he asked, contrasting this with satellite imagery showing damage at 13 Pakistani air bases.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who released a separate documentary on the operation's first anniversary in May 2026, described Operation Sindoor as "not merely a military operation but a living testament to India's whole-of-government approach."

What's Next

The Discovery premiere arrives as India marks Independence Day and continues to navigate the aftermath of the India-Pakistan standoff. Defence analyst John Spencer of West Point has called the operation a watershed moment in India's counterterrorism doctrine, noting it marked a shift from retaliation to deterrence.
nri_angle: The docuseries premieres on India's Independence Day, a milestone widely celebrated by the Indian diaspora, and offers the most detailed public account yet of the decision-making behind Operation Sindoor.
